fact: UNDP says it deployed country-hosted AI compute capacity in South Africa under its AI Infrastructure Activation programme.
UNDP's programme procured and deployed country-hosted GPU compute in South Africa.
Vodacom group CTO Dejan Kastelic told Business Day that South Africa will be the last of three large markets where Vodacom plans to install GPUs, starting small and mainly for internal use.

The Stellenbosch University Policy Innovation Lab lists among South African AI tools in deployment the CSIR body and number plate recognition system and the University of Johannesburg facial recognition access control.

fact: The University of Cape Town reports that its team developed MzansiText, a multilingual dataset of South Africa's 11 official written languages, and MzansiLM, a 125-million-parameter language model trained on it from scratch, and made both publicly available.

The University of Cape Town says its African Compute Initiative, funded under the GBP 58 million AI4D programme of the UK FCDO and Canada's IDRC, will build a GPU cluster for AI research in UCT's High Performance Computing Data Centre, targeted to be operational within 12 months.
HPE says Mzansi Mind, a Solcon Capital sovereign enterprise AI platform, runs its Siya language model supporting all official South African languages on HPE servers hosted in Johannesburg.
HPE says Mzansi Mind's inferencing environment uses HPE ProLiant DL380a Gen12 servers with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, hosted at Equinix's Johannesburg colocation data centre.

The science minister's reply says the CSIR has taken delivery of a new 4 petaflop high-performance computing system for the NICIS, which supports AI among other uses, with phase 1 expected live by end November 2026 and completion by end March 2027.

UCT reports that researchers at four universities, backed by the NRF and the Telkom Centres of Excellence programme, are developing large language models for isiXhosa, isiZulu and Sepedi in a project running until 2027.

fact: The Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation's written reply says InkubaLM, a South African-developed large language model for low-resource African languages created by Lelapa AI, has emerged from privately or donor-funded work, while no government-backed home-grown LLM is being developed.

The NICIS CHPC service catalogue lists a Dell peta-scale HPC and GPU cluster with 30 Nvidia V100 GPU nodes and 4 PB of storage as a service, with use cases that include enabling machine learning insights.
The CHPC GPU cluster is offered free for six-month renewable periods to academic and public-interest users and for a fee to commercial users, with over 2000 users and over a billion core hours used.
